 Follow Pixar proves that, yes, Mafia cats can still be cute in new Gatto trailer
 William Hughes Thu, November 12, 2026 at 11:30 PM UTC 1 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. We've been keeping an eye on Pixar's latest film,  Gatto , for more than a year now , as  Luca   director Enrico Casarosa assembled a typically star-studded voice cast—including Mark Ruffalo and Laurence Fishburne—to tell a story that feels like an obvious slam dunk for the studio, about a Venetian kitty cat who finds himself torn by his (nine) lives in feline organized crime. Now, after an earlier tease, Pixar has released a full trailer for the film, putting its Mafia kitty cat antics on full display.
 The most eye-catching things about Gatto don't turn out to be its feline subjects, though. Instead, it's how they're animated; for the first time in what feels like a long time, Pixar has moved away from its usual clean CGI style to something far sketchier, and far livelier—suggesting that not even Disney's resident hitmakers are immune to animation trends that films like Across The Spider-Verse  have been dipping into in recent years. The upshot is to create something that's probably Pixar's most interesting visual palette since  Soul , even if the actual storytelling—cat torn between past loyalties and future happiness, with a patina of death hanging over everything—feels pretty Pixar-familiar.
 Gatto  arrives in theaters on March 5, 2027; it'll arrive after a year that's reportedly been a tough one at the studio, as it struggles to launch movies that aren't ensconced inside existing franchises like  Toy Story  and  Inside Out .
